desc: Offline Linux nvme-apple port for T6040 based on yuka feature/m4-m5-nvme: ad8908064 (apple,t8132-nvme-ans2, separate mmio_nvmmu, M4 IOQ pointer regs, M4 hw descriptor) + 1b87d7b84 (T6041 DT: three-region reg nvme=reg[9] 0x4dcc0000/0x10000, ans mailbox 0x09600000/0x4000, nvmmu=reg[3] 0x0dcc0000/0x60000; reg-names nvme/ans/nvmmu; apple,sart, 4 mailbox irqs, ANS/APCIE power-domains, ANS reset). NOT a blind copy: her M4/M5 commits are marked untested and 9a6a6bd18 disables Set Features/Number-of-Queues because it CRASHES ANS on 26.x. Preserve the reg[3] caveat (not a clean NVMMU-only window: +0x1300 readable, +0x1210 faulted 07-25). Open anomaly to carry: delete sq/cq returns status 2 = Invalid Field (NOT Invalid Opcode) - lead is M4 queue-state/teardown-order around the IOQ pointer regs. Adapt DT numbers from OUR captured ADT, not t6041 copy-paste. NO live writes or boots until separately reviewed. PROGRESS 2026-07-30: yuka ad890806+9a6a6bd1+3b6b20a8 cherry-picked to wallace/t6040-bringup; t6040 DT node written from OUR ADT (irqs match t6041; sart 0xc000; old single-base node REPLACED); NVME_APPLE=y (APPLE_SART=m pin fixed); v3 object 65f6fbe3 packed+allowlisted. First boot = first live nvme-apple probe on T6040; dual-mode+rollback is the net. FIRST BOOT RESULT (v4, 2026-07-30): driver+DT proven through identify + 3-namespace enumeration, then ANS FIRMWARE crashed -- wake-path-into-live-iBoot-ANS root cause (our loader lacks m1n1 nvme_shutdown). Kernel fix patches/t6040-nvme-apple-force-clean-ans-boot.patch forces the clean boot path; v5 object 16a4c594. Upstream-relevant robustness patch + the m1n1 nvme_ensure_shutdown gap both drafted for CJ. v5 RESULT: kernel-side cold yank also fails (BOOT_STATUS never OK; dead-ctrl removal + blk_mq_release teardown splat). v6: quiesce in the m1n1 PREFIX via nvme_ensure_shutdown (init-then-shutdown, the 174-proven sequence) on branch wallace/t6040-pcie-nvme-dualmode, prefix 165cf405, object 2abc4901. v6 RESULT (2026-07-30, serial dmesg): m1n1 quiesce WORKS -- clean cold RTKit boot under Linux, nvme0n1 enumerated with p1-p4 (p4 = CJ 128GiB exFAT), partition table READ off the internal SSD. Then fw assert: "[7454]: CQ (Host I/O) DB error, status_reg 0x4, head 61, valid_status 0x4, err_info_0 0x3, err_info_1 0x40000" during the partition-scan I/O burst (m1n1 never hit it: 1-2 cmds, no head march). Discriminator built: t8132 max_queue_depth 64->16 (76da12a3); depth-related -> works at 16; wrap-semantics -> crashes faster near 13-15. One chainload cycle needed. Draft for yuka/CJ regardless of outcome. v7 DISCRIMINATOR RESULT (2026-07-30): depth 16 -> assert at head 15 (wrap boundary; was 61 at depth 64; err_info scales with depth). CQ wrap/doorbell semantics broken on fw 26.5 fw-managed queues — not a depth limit. E1 next (proxy-only over rollback): extend t6040-nvme-probe.py to ~200 sequential LBA reads, marching m1n1 own ioq through wraps. m1n1 crashes too -> fw RE (CoastGuard); m1n1 survives -> diff m1n1-vs-Linux completion path (suspect: head doorbell off-by-one fatal only near wrap). CJ enrolls rollback; campaign = chainloads only. E1 RESULT (2026-07-30, transcript 12b1a20b): m1n1 wrap-march 200 reads / ~3 CQ wraps PASSED — wraps per se are fine, bug is in the Linux-vs-m1n1 diff. E2 RESULT (batched CQ doorbell emulated in m1n1, skip 3 of 4 DB writes so the 4th jumps head by 4): ALSO PASSED — batched/jumping doorbell REFUTED as the trigger. Remaining structural diff: CONCURRENCY. m1n1 always uses tag 0 with exactly ONE command outstanding; Linux keeps many tags in flight, so multiple CQEs land per poll and TCB invalidations interleave with head advancement. Next: E3 = multi-tag/multi-outstanding emulation in m1n1 (real work: nvme_exec_command is synchronous single-tag), or cheaper first pass = force Linux to depth 2 (one outstanding I/O + admin) and see if the assert disappears; if it does, concurrency confirmed and the fix is likely ordering (TCB inval vs DB) rather than depth. E3 (depth 2): INCONCLUSIVE — driver never probes at depth 2 (no nvme-apple messages at all, only pmgr sync_state pending); depth restored to 64. E4 (acknowledge every CQE immediately instead of once per drained batch): REFUTED as a fix, but sharpened the picture — crash head moved 61 -> 63 at depth 64, i.e. with eager acking Linux survives to the LAST slot and dies exactly AT the wrap (depth 16 died at 15 = same pattern). Combined with E1 (m1n1 wraps 3x fine), the fault is Linux-specific wrap handling. Next candidates: (a) the t8132 need_ioq_register path writing ioq cq/sq DMA bases to 0x1208/0x1200 — yuka newest least-tested code, and if the fw ring base/size differs from what Linux assumes, the wrap lands out of range; (b) phase-bit convention at the flip; (c) whether the fw honors create_cq qsize at all. Also worth trying: does the fw accept a non-power-of-2 or smaller create_cq qsize while Linux keeps depth 64 bookkeeping? E5/E5b: tagset queue_depth 1 is an INVALID tagset (reserved_tags=2 > total) and 3 also hangs the boot with no console output — restricted tagsets break boot before console init, cause unknown, blocks the clean concurrency test. Full evidence chain + excluded hypotheses in done/2026-07-30-t6040-nvme-linux-wrap-assert-E1-E5.md. E6 (register diff, read-only dump from working m1n1, transcript linux-build-out/e6-regdump-m1n1.txt): the 0x249xx linear-SQ block lives in the CONTROLLER aperture reg[9] (LINEAR_SQ_CTRL reads 1 there; m1n1 rings reg[9]+0x2490c/0x24910 and works; reg[3]+0x24908 is the 07-25 SError address). Linux points sq_db at mmio_nvmmu (reg[3]) while cq_db is at mmio_nvme (reg[9]) — SQ and CQ doorbells for the same queue in DIFFERENT windows. Invisible pre-M4 (same mapping), real with the two-base split. E7 = point sq_db at mmio_nvme: built and booted but produced NO console output (same signature as E5/E5b), so UNTESTED not refuted; needs a panel watch (console=tty0) to read. E7 (sq_db->mmio_nvme, stock window): boots clean, NVMe silent after RTKit init — 0x24910 is outside the 0x10000 nvme resource so the write never lands; this also explains yukas mmio_nvmmu choice (she needed the 0x60000 SIZE, not the base). E8 (same + window widened to 0x60000): CONFIRMED HANG. So Linux writing reg[9]+0x24910 through a real ioremap is fatal while m1n1 writes the same address happily -> difference is access CONTEXT (nonposted-mmio, DART, live IRQs) not address. Next: compare m1n1 MMU mapping of that page vs devm_platform_ioremap_resource, and try posted mapping (ioremap vs ioremap_np / reg outside the nonposted-mmio parent) for that window only. ALSO: the earlier E5/E5b/E7 no-console-output boots were a HOST-side kisd/reader problem, not hangs — re-attach and prove the console before calling a hang. Both experiments REVERTED; tree and /out are back to the known-good baseline.
